visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video opens with a medium shot of a woman with auburn hair wearing a white sweater and grey jeans. She is standing in a brightly lit kitchen with white cabinets. She holds a smartphone with a pink case toward the camera, displaying an SMS message. A large orange text overlay asks if this is a new scam technique. (2) A quick cut to a grayscale filter shows the woman's face in a close-up as she looks suspicious and confused, maintaining the previous text overlay. (3) The scene returns to color as she continues talking and gesturing. In the background, white shoes and a brown box sit on the floor of what appears to be a living area or entryway. (4) A close-up of the phone screen reveals a message from the sender '935199' concerning a 'time message' from 2020. An Instagram notification for '@fangyu_muggle' appears at the top. (5) The woman reacts with high energy, and the text 'Really?!' appears in Chinese. A woman in a black floral dress walks in the background. (6) The scene shifts to a man in a white 'Hogwarts' sweatshirt sitting at a desk. He holds a phone and shows a Google search screen for 'Taiwan Mobile' and 'Open Possible' to verify the sender. (7) Back to the woman, she looks at her phone while a 'loading' icon is superimposed on her head, indicating she is thinking. She decides to click the link. (8) The phone screen displays a Christmas-themed webpage with the title 'Time Message: Open Possible'. (9) Realizing it was a message she wrote to herself, the woman laughs heartily while holding the phone. Two other people are seen laughing in the background. (10) The video ends with a close-up of a second woman in a white beret laughing and covering her mouth, with celebratory text appearing on screen.

narrative_and_purpose.narrativeStructure: Montage -> Linear: Hook -> Conflict -> Investigation -> Reveal -> Resolution
narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video uses a humorous storytelling format to promote a 'Time Message' service from Taiwan Mobile. It begins with a hook about potential scams to grab attention, transitions into a mock investigation, and ends with a sentimental and funny reveal that the 'scam' was actually a message sent by the creator to her future self.
